title: Acute Heart Failure and Pulmonary Oedema

pathophysiology.summary: Raised filling pressures cause pulmonary or systemic venous congestion; impaired output and neurohormonal activation can worsen renal sodium retention. Acute triggers may include ischaemia, arrhythmia, infection, uncontrolled blood pressure, medication interruption, or renal deterioration. Clinical decisions should align with current Saudi guidance, local pathways, and individual clinical assessment.

impaired output and neurohormonal activation can worsen renal sodium retention. Acute triggers may include ischaemia, arrhythmia, infection, uncontrolled blood pressure, medication interruption, or renal deterioration.

actions: Use the topic-specific focus in this record to agree immediate and longer-term priorities with the patient.

actions: Confirm a feasible follow-up date and contact route.

pathophysiology.summary: Toxicity depends on the substance, dose, formulation, time, co-ingestants, and host physiology. Absorption and metabolism may cause delayed injury, and initially reassuring observations do not exclude later deterioration. Clinical decisions should align with current Saudi guidance, local pathways, and individual clinical assessment.
keyMechanisms: Toxicity depends on the substance, dose, formulation, time, co-ingestants, and host physiology. Absorption and metabolism may cause delayed injury, and initially reassuring observations do not exclude later deterioration.
Clinical expression and progression vary with baseline risk, comorbidity, treatment exposure, and access to timely care.

symptoms: Evaluate the characteristic symptom pattern of Acute Poisoning and Overdose, including onset, evolution, severity, associated symptoms, precipitating factors, complications, and relevant negative findings.
Clarify onset, progression, associated symptoms, baseline function, medicines and the patient’s own priorities.
Clarify the chronology, severity, associated features, relevant exposures, and risk factors; document important negative findings rather than assuming their absence.
physicalSigns: Assess vital signs and perform a focused examination relevant to Acute Poisoning and Overdose and its important differentials.
Assess functional change, comorbidity, hydration/perfusion where relevant, and baseline status.
Use serial reassessment when the condition or treatment can change over hours or days.
redFlags: Airway compromise or respiratory depression
Seizure, dysrhythmia, shock, or severe acidosis
Hyperthermia or rapidly changing consciousness
High-risk caustic/cardiotoxic exposure or delayed-release ingestion

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: May mimic intoxication and require parallel evaluation.
Look for occult injury.
Timing and substance history distinguish toxicity from withdrawal.

ruleIn.testName: Bedside glucose, ECG, vital-sign trends, and targeted laboratory tests based on exposure and toxidrome.
ruleIn.targetCondition: Acute Poisoning and Overdose
ruleIn.expectedFinding: A result that supports the working diagnosis or defines its severity, interpreted with the clinical picture and current criteria.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Choose this investigation because it can confirm the suspected process, establish baseline risk, or change a diagnostic or management decision.

ruleIn.testName: Contact regional poison centre or toxicologist; broad screening should not replace focused assessment.
ruleIn.targetCondition: Cause, complication, or risk relevant to Acute Poisoning and Overdose
ruleIn.expectedFinding: A result that may identify a precipitating factor or complication; interpret in context rather than as a stand-alone diagnosis.
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: This helps detect an important alternative or complication and informs safe monitoring and referral.

ruleOut.testName: Focused evaluation for the leading alternative diagnoses
ruleOut.targetCondition: Important alternative to Acute Poisoning and Overdose
ruleOut.expectedFinding: Findings that lower the likelihood of the selected alternative; a normal result does not exclude every urgent cause.
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: The differential matters because it changes urgency or treatment and should be actively considered.

ruleOut.testName: Serial clinical reassessment with targeted repeat testing when indicated
ruleOut.expectedFinding: Stable or improving clinical trend without new evidence of the suspected complication.
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: A single early assessment may miss an evolving problem; repeat only when it can guide care.

actions: Confirm the presenting concern, relevant timeline, baseline function, medicines, allergies, comorbidities, and the patient’s immediate priorities.

branches.condition: A red flag, instability, or rapid deterioration is present
actions: Escalate immediately to the responsible senior or emergency team using the local pathway.

branches.condition: The person is stable for a planned or longitudinal pathway
actions: Proceed with focused assessment and shared planning.

clinicalManagement.title: Confirm the working diagnosis and stratify risk
clinicalManagement.timeframe: Promptly; adapt timing to acuity
actions: Use the history, examination, and investigations listed above to confirm the likely process and assess important alternatives.

branches.condition: The diagnosis remains uncertain or tests conflict with the clinical picture
actions: Reassess the history and examination and seek senior or specialty advice.

actions: Switch to the relevant urgent or specialty pathway.
Communicate the finding and handover responsibility clearly.
